expected: The durable LocalSIM execution-state authority closes over the frozen plan, restart/recovery, and the legal lifecycle epoch. Post-close terminalization deterministically selects only contract-authorized state authority, reaches the correct run terminal state, rejects genuine duplicate/corrupt/missing/extra/identity-drift evidence, and one binding failure does not block other scheduler bindings.
fix_summary: LocalSIM lifecycle and economic readback reuse one strict durable authority closure over current run identity, continuous receipt generations, the generation high-watermark, exact receipt/outbox identities, and the committed state_id-to-state_hash set. Empty authority now also requires every economic/projection generation carrier to be absent; orphan outbox/receipt/generation or broker-side-effect facts fail loud without terminalizing the damaged run, while independent bindings continue. PostgreSQL evidence comes from committed guarded DEV rows read through real repository connections and independent post-commit readback.
non_goals: Do not start, stop, or restart any user backend without explicit per-target approval.
root_cause: The original lifecycle closure collapsed state_id-keyed history into an intent_id map and treated legal terminal incarnations as duplicate current writers. The first PR repair then left strict authority/readback gaps, and the next review found that the empty-state/empty-receipt branch still returned generation zero while orphan projection/economic carriers remained. The prior PostgreSQL-labelled tests also monkeypatched an InMemory daily-run getter, so they did not prove committed PostgreSQL row JSON or independent post-commit readback.
